dsh-mnemon-embedding.version: dsh-mnemon 0.5.45 (commit 1dec529); Memory Spaces 0.5.27, Mnemon Native provider 0.5.11, Layered strategy 0.5.13; mnemon CLI 0.2.13
dsh-mnemon-embedding.mode: default backend Mnemon Native (mnemon CLI, SQLite graph) with its optional embedding mode switched on (config embedding.enabled, shared bge-m3 endpoint); verbatim exact writes through service.remember (no LLM review step); default quality policy strict-v1
dsh-mnemon-embedding.how: write: MemorySpacesService.remember({content}) -> MnemonNativeProvider.remember -> `mnemon remember <content> --cat general --imp 3 --source user`; ranked: MemorySpacesService.search({query, limit:10, inspect:true}) with recallQuality policy exhaustive-v1 -> MnemonNativeProvider.search -> `mnemon --readonly recall <q> --limit 40 --verbose` (+ service lexical recovery via `mnemon search` when no anchor evidence); deployed: createThreeTierTurn(view).query() recall route (Layered strategy retrieval.ts: limit 6, admission of <=4 results / 3600 chars / <=1 medium / <=1 unknown, low tier dropped) over MemorySpacesService.search with default policy strict-v1 (low 0.25, high 0.6, candidate pool 18, `mnemon recall --verbose` live, access recorded)
notes: Backend: the default Provider of dsh-mnemon is Mnemon Native, a thin driver over the separate `mnemon` CLI (npm @mnemon-dev/mnemon 0.2.13, Go binary, SQLite). dsh-mnemon itself holds no retrieval index for Memory Spaces; the CLI returns scored candidates and dsh-mnemon applies its quality policy and per-turn admission.

Write path: the default product write path is an LLM-driven idle review / distillation that decides what to store. No LLM budget: memories were written verbatim through the explicit remember API (service.remember, defaults category=general, importance=3, source=user, no tags/entities). The review step was bypassed and is not measured. llm_tokens=0.

Dates: `mnemon remember` has no date argument (created_at = now). Memories were written in date order within seconds; the memory dates are not represented in the store, so any recency/temporal signal of the CLI sees all memories as written at the same moment.
Dedup/conflict detection of the CLI stayed on. Actions returned by remember: {"added":240}. Rows stored: 240 of 240.

ranked uses a second service instance configured with the built-in policy exhaustive-v1 (no score threshold, no tier caps), limit 10, inspect=true (readonly snapshot). Items that carry score 0 are still listed in CLI order. The CLI itself fetches a pool of 40 for smart recall; with embeddings the driver re-ranks that pool by vector similarity.

deployed = the model-facing first Recall call of one turn under the default Layered strategy. dsh-mnemon does NOT inject Memory Space recall automatically before a turn; the model has to call the recall tool (the resident runtime-memory source, which is separate hot memory and is not benchmarked, is the only thing always injected). A quiet question therefore only returns nothing if the model calls recall and the policy admits nothing; a model might also skip the call.
deployed scores are 0 for every item: the strategy admission (boundedModelInsights) drops the score field before the model sees the result; order is the admitted order.

deployed ms covers the whole strategy read (service.search incl. the `mnemon` process launches, any lexical-recovery call, admission), measured around that call only. Each launch is a new process (node launcher -> native binary).

Ordering side effect: deployed runs a live (non-readonly) recall, which records access counts for returned candidates and may influence later questions, as in real use; ranked runs first, readonly, on the same state. Questions were run in id order.

Host glue stubbed: View/ReadGrant objects, the Source recall-route evidence() wrapper (copied logic: limit, 16000-char budget, provenance incl. relevanceTier), `dsh-mnemon` core helper barrel (real input.ts / storage-lock.ts), cordis/Loader (not needed). Nothing of the CLI, the driver, the quality policy or the strategy admission is reimplemented.
Write failures: 0. Question failures: 0. Returned items that could not be mapped to a memory id: 0. embed-missing fill result: {"memoryBodyId":"default","filled":0,"remaining":0,"model":"bge-m3"}.

caveat.zh: 同 dsh-mnemon，打开了可选的向量模式（bge-m3）；每次运行约 ±5 个百分点波动；LLM 复盘被绕过。
caveat.en: As dsh-mnemon with the optional embedding mode switched on (bge-m3); about ±5 points run to run; the LLM review is bypassed.

feiyu-memgate-embedding-bge-base-zh.mode: verbatim ingest, embedding backend (hf.co/CompendiumLabs/bge-base-zh-v1.5-gguf:Q8_0 via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, brute-force cosine), default recall stages, no LLM
feiyu-memgate-embedding-bge-base-zh.how: config.build_gateway(dict); EmbeddingBackend.put_many([(text, id, date)]) once for all memories; Gateway.recall('owner', {'query': q}) for deployed; EmbeddingBackend.find(query, 10) for ranked
notes: Backend is the embedding backend: model hf.co/CompendiumLabs/bge-base-zh-v1.5-gguf:Q8_0, cosine mapped to 0..1 with floor 0.35 and ceil 0.80 (the backend's values for this model, chosen on the development sets, not on this data); query prefix set, document prefix none.
ranked scores are the mapped relevance values, not comparable across systems.

deployed uses the default recall stages (min_score with the backend's default 0.25, relative_score with the backend's default ratio 0.75, fill_text, drop_oversize, redact, dedupe, budget) and the default limit of 5; ms times that Gateway.recall call only.
Deployed items are reported by the id field of each recall item; 0 item(s) named no dataset memory.
0 recall call(s) did not answer 200; 0 ranked search(es) failed.
deployed was timed before ranked, so ms includes the real query embedding request; ranked then reuses the backend's query-embedding cache.
Gateway.recall was called directly, so the per-client rate limiter (applied only in admit) was not involved.
Memories were ingested with one put_many call (embedding requests of 32 texts); ingest_seconds covers it.

feiyu-memgate-full.mode: verbatim ingest with dates, hybrid backend (sqlite keyword + embedding bge-m3, probabilistic-OR fusion), default recall stages plus freshness, forgetting ledger with default settings, no sweep, no LLM
feiyu-memgate-full.how: config.build_gateway(dict with [forgetting]); HybridBackend.put_many([(text, id, date)]) once; Forgetting.sync('private', store); Gateway.recall('owner', {'query': q}) for deployed (stages: min_score, freshness, relative_score, fill_text, drop_oversize, redact, dedupe, budget); HybridBackend.find(query, 10) scored by the freshness stage's prepare() for ranked
notes: Backend is the hybrid backend: a sqlite keyword child (IDF-weighted containment of character bigrams and CJK single characters) and an embedding child (bge-m3, cosine mapped with floor 0.40 and ceil 0.80); fused score = 1 - prod(1 - score_i) with both weights 1.0. Defaults chosen on the development sets, not on this data.

Everything is turned on with documented defaults: stages min_score, freshness (floor 0.7), relative_score, fill_text, drop_oversize, redact, dedupe, budget; [forgetting] with the default Ebbinghaus curve, a temporary ledger and archive; no sweep was run and nothing was forgotten.

Memories carry their own dates; Forgetting.sync made each ledger first_seen the memory's date. The forgetting clock was pinned to the day after the newest memory so the run does not depend on today's date.
ranked is the backend's top 10 with freshness applied (prepare() only, no use recorded); no threshold.
Uses recorded by each deployed recall were removed again and the ledger re-synchronised, so every question was asked of the same state.
deployed uses the default limit of 5; ms times that Gateway.recall call only (two children, then freshness reads the ledger).
Deployed items are reported by the id field of each recall item; 0 item(s) named no dataset memory.
0 recall call(s) did not answer 200; 0 ranked search(es) failed.
deployed was timed before ranked, so ms includes the real query embedding request; ranked then reuses the backend's query-embedding cache.
Gateway.recall was called directly, so the per-client rate limiter (applied only in admit) was not involved.
Memories were ingested with one put_many call (embedding requests of 32 texts); ingest_seconds covers it.

feiyu-memgate-openviking.mode: verbatim memory-file ingest into OpenViking, feiyu-memgate openviking backend (read-only store), default recall stages, bge-m3 embeddings inside OpenViking, no LLM
feiyu-memgate-openviking.how: config.build_gateway(dict); OpenVikingBackend.put(text, ref=viking://~/memories/events/Y/M/D/<id>.md) per memory; OpenVikingBackend.find(query, 10) for ranked; Gateway.recall('owner', {'query': q}) for deployed; id = file name of the item's URI
notes: Memories written with OpenVikingBackend.put (content/write, mode create) as memory files, no session or extraction, so no language model is used; llm_tokens is 0. Ingest went into its own OpenViking user.
ingest_seconds includes the wait until a sample of 21 memories (and the last one written) found themselves (wait 67.4 s; writes alone 2.4 s, 0 put failure(s)).
ranked: backend.find(query, 10) of the read-only store; directory summaries (.abstract.md, .overview.md) are skipped by the backend itself, so ranked can hold fewer than 10 items.

deployed uses the default recall stages (min_score, relative_score, newer_first, fill_text, drop_oversize, redact, dedupe, budget) and the default limit of 5; the gateway asks the backend for 15 candidates; ms times that Gateway.recall call only. The backend maps OpenViking's raw score with its default floor 0.50 / ceil 1.00 (raw kept in Hit.meta); its defaults are min_score 0.55 and relative ratio 0.95, so min_score 0.55 means raw 0.775.
Backend and gateway timeouts are the defaults (backend socket timeout 2 s) except for ingest writes (30 s).
Recall item ids: the memory id is the file name of the item's URI (id field); 0 item(s) unmapped.
0 recall call(s) did not answer 200; 0 backend find call(s) for ranked failed.
Gateway.recall was called directly, so the per-client rate limiter was not involved.

feiyu-memgate-sqlite-broad.mode: verbatim ingest, sqlite keyword backend (IDF-weighted grams), default recall stages with the broad profile, no embeddings, no LLM
feiyu-memgate-sqlite-broad.how: config.build_gateway(dict); SQLiteBackend.put(text, ref, date) per memory; SQLiteBackend.find(query, 10) for ranked; Gateway.recall('owner', {'query': q}) for deployed
notes: Backend is the sqlite keyword backend: IDF-weighted containment of character bigrams and CJK single characters (a gram's weight is its BM25 inverse document frequency in the store); it does not understand meaning, so paraphrase questions are expected to be weak.
ranked scores are the backend's own weighted-containment values, not comparable across systems.

graphiti.mode: LLM extraction (deepseek-flash, JSON mode) of entities and temporal facts into embedded Kuzu; bge-m3 embeddings; 240 of 240 memories ingested
graphiti.how: Graphiti(graph_driver=KuzuDriver, llm_client=OpenAIGenericClient(json_object), embedder=OpenAIEmbedder(bge-m3)).add_episode(name=id, episode_body=text, reference_time=date, default group (no group_id)) per memory; Graphiti.search(query) (EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF, limit 10) for ranked and deployed
notes: INGESTED 240 of 240 memories as episodes (name = memory id); failed episodes: 0; not ingested: 0. If this is below 240 it is a SUBSET: the 127 memories that are expect/stale for some question were taken first, the remaining ones in date order while the 5 CNY budget lasted. The scorer still scores all 160 questions, so questions whose memories were not ingested cannot be answered.
Failed episode ids: none

ranked and deployed are the SAME call: Graphiti.search(query) = recipe EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF (BM25 + cosine over facts, RRF), default limit 10. The recipe applies its own default cosine floor (sim_min_score 0.6, search_utils.DEFAULT_MIN_SCORE) and has no token budget, so deployed = ranked = its default result and ms times that call (1 embedding request + Kuzu queries, no LLM).

Returned items are fact edges. Mapping: an edge maps to the memory of the earliest episode in edge.episodes (by memory date); several edges from one memory keep the best position; unmappable -> null. search() returns no scores, so score = 1/rank (order only).
Invalidated facts: of 58 edges returned over all questions, 1 had invalid_at/expired_at set (search() does not filter superseded edges).
Graph at the end: {"entity_edges": 69, "edges_with_invalid_at": 1, "entity_nodes": 125, "episodes": 240}

LLM: deepseek-flash via OpenAIGenericClient(structured_output_mode='json_object', max_tokens=8192); embedder bge-m3 1024d; cross-encoder = pass-through stub (Graphiti default needs an OpenAI model; unused by search()). Kuzu embedded driver (deprecated upstream, still shipped).

LLM calls: 596 (0 errored), prompt tokens 1028457 (cache hit 151040), completion tokens 148062. llm_cost_cny is the DeepSeek balance difference incl. 0.12 CNY of earlier debugging runs (2.0; other workers may have spent concurrently); token-based estimate at assumed prices (2.0 in / 8.0 out CNY per M): 3.2414.
Budget stop reached: False. Query failures: 0. ingest_seconds sums add_episode wall-clock over 240 episodes (the graph grows during ingest).

Every episode is text-typed (EpisodeType.text), default group (no group_id: KuzuDriver in 0.31.2 lacks the _database attribute that an explicit group_id needs), reference_time = memory date 00:00 UTC; only text, date and id were given to the system.

caveat.zh: 非推荐的技术栈：嵌入式 Kuzu（上游已标记弃用）+ 一个小 LLM（deepseek-flash）做提取，中文单句记忆；总共约 118 万 tokens；返回的是提取出的事实边，不是原文。
caveat.en: Non-recommended stack: embedded Kuzu (deprecated upstream) + a small LLM (deepseek-flash) for extraction, on one-sentence Chinese memories; about 1.18 M tokens; it returns extracted fact edges, not the original text.

lingshu-dsh-memory.mode: verbatim user messages through the plugin hook (regex redaction on, forgetting gate on), md_cg lexical/BM25 retrieval, no embeddings, no LLM; deployed = default automatic injection
lingshu-dsh-memory.how: resolveToken + new MdcgClient(...) (MCP stdio to python -m md_cg.mcp_server); ingest: installMemoryHooks session/event handler (user/message) -> desensitize -> MdcgClient.remember -> mdcg_remember(gated=true); ranked: MdcgClient.read(query,{k:10}) = cg(op=read); deployed: installMemoryHooks system-prompt/assemble handler (lingshu:auto-recall timeline block + lingshu:session-window block)
notes: Ingest pacing: the plugin's default write cap is 8 writes per 60 s per layer/role (excess is DEFERred, not stored; env MDCG_WRITELIMIT=0 would disable it). The cap was left at its default and writes were paced 7600 ms apart; ingest_seconds is the time spent in the write calls only (4.1 s); total wall clock including the pacing sleeps was 1829 s.

Ingest: every memory was sent as one user/message event through the plugin's own session/event hook (installMemoryHooks), which redacts with its regex list, then calls MdcgClient.remember -> MCP mdcg_remember(gated=true, layer=contextual, dedupe=true). It also fires a read (k=3) and a short-window write per message, as in production. Memory date is not passed: the hook path has no date field (write time is used).

Write gate verdicts over the 240 memories (the hook lets the forgetting gate decide ACCEPT/MERGE/DROP/DEFER): {"ACCEPT":240}. First receipt shape: {"ok":true,"x":{"verdict":"ACCEPT","node_id":"mem_1794669517228_dc9c2e","gate":{"verdict":"ACCEPT","reason":"重要度 0.60≥0.3","redundancy":{"max":0,"with":null,"jaccard":0,"compared":0},"importance":{"score":0.6,"from":"hint"},"entropy":{"source_kind":"external_surprising","novelty":1,"self_information_bits":4,"normalized":1,"duplicate_with":null,"duplicate_ratio":0,"compared":0,"overwrite_of":null,"overwrite_ratio":null},"dedup_skipped":null},"written":"mem_1794669517228_dc9c2e","consistency":{"t":1794669517.2310362,"layer":"contextual","verdict":"BLINDSPOT","reason":"既有节点均未声明条件：无法建立比对路径","confl
Memories changed by the write-path redaction (desensitize, default on): 0 [].
ranked = MdcgClient.read(query,{k:10}) = MCP cg(op=read, query, k=10) (BM25 path of search_rrf, no threshold). cg/stg is the only tool surface exposed by default (tools: "core").

deployed = what the per-turn system-prompt/assemble hook injects with default settings: the "lingshu:auto-recall" block (timeline of the 4 newest non-identity nodes of the session, 1400-char cap, decayed per-item 160/144/130/117 chars) PLUS the "lingshu:session-window" block (last 10 messages of the session, 900-char cap). Neither block uses the question: the hook never passes the query to retrieval. Items from both blocks are mapped to memory ids by text and merged (timeline first).
deployed item counts per question: min 4 max 4; distinct deployed lists across 160 questions: 1. Block names seen in total: {"lingshu:auto-recall":161,"lingshu:session-window":161}.

All 240 memories were placed in ONE session (the benchmark has no sessions); the injection is session-scoped, so this is the best case for it. A fresh hook instance was used per question so the per-session "max 2 injections per item" cap (issue #739) starts clean.
Both injected blocks are wrapped in the plugin's own header and footer lines; those wrapper lines are skipped when mapping.
Unmapped items (id null): ranked 0, deployed 0. Failed calls: 0.
Timings are for the assemble handler call only (it includes two round trips to the Python brain: timeline and session recall).

caveat.zh: 按设计每轮自动注入的是会话里最新的 4 条，不看问题，所以“交付命中”为 0 是设计使然，不是检索失败；排名用的是它的 BM25 读取。
caveat.en: By design the per-turn injection is the 4 newest items of the session and ignores the question, so a deployed hit of 0 follows from the design, not from failed retrieval; the ranking uses its BM25 read.

memsearch.mode: verbatim Markdown ingest (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md), hybrid dense+BM25 on Milvus Lite, bge-m3 embeddings via OpenAI-compatible endpoint, no LLM, no reranker
memsearch.how: CLI `memsearch index <memory dir> --provider openai --model bge-m3 --base-url <embedder>/v1` for ingest; memsearch.core.MemSearch.search(query, top_k=10) for ranked; MemSearch.search(query, top_k=5) for deployed (the DSH memory-recall skill's `memsearch search --top-k 5`); chunk -> memory id via the '<!-- id:mNNN -->' anchor in chunk content
notes: Installed from the scanned source checkout (commit 369ae1da48b7, pyproject version 0.4.23) with pip inside the image build.

Ingest: memories written as Markdown, memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, one '### 00:NN' section per memory plus an '<!-- id:mNNN -->' anchor line; indexed with the CLI `memsearch index` (default chunking: 1500 chars, split on headings). Every chunk therefore holds exactly one memory; the id is read from the anchor in the returned chunk content. The HH:MM heading values are a per-day sequence, not real times. The memory text is verbatim; no source/kind fields used.
ingest_seconds covers writing the Markdown files plus the `memsearch index` subprocess (python start-up, embedding via the shared bge-m3 endpoint, Milvus Lite insert).
Embeddings: provider 'openai' with base_url http://fmg-bench-embedder:11434/v1, model bge-m3 (memsearch's documented OpenAI-compatible setting). Dimension auto-detected (1024).
Search is memsearch's default hybrid retrieval (dense COSINE + BM25 fused by RRF k=60, score normalised to 0..1); no reranker (default off), no threshold exists in the library.

ranked = MemSearch.search(query, top_k=10). deployed = MemSearch.search(query, top_k=5): the DSH plugin has no automatic injection (it only adds a reminder to use the memory-recall skill); that skill runs `memsearch search "<q>" --top-k 5 --json-output`, with no score threshold and no character budget. The CLI calls the same MemSearch.search; it was called in-process so `ms` excludes CLI process start-up (a few seconds of python/pymilvus import per CLI call in real use).
In the real plugin the agent decides whether to search and writes its own query text; here the benchmark question is passed verbatim.
Not used (default off / needs an LLM): compact/summarise, plugin turn capture, maintenance tasks, reranker, file watcher.
0 chunk(s) could not be mapped to a memory id; 0 query failure(s).

caveat.zh: Markdown 入库，稠密 + BM25 的 RRF 融合；没有阈值和字数预算，交付 = 前 5 条；插件本身不自动注入，是否检索由模型决定。
caveat.en: Markdown ingest, dense + BM25 fused by RRF; no threshold or character budget, delivered = top 5; the plugin does not inject automatically, the model decides whether to search.

meow-memory.mode: verbatim ingest through memory_remember (level fact, global scope, importance 1), keywords derived by the plugin's tokenizer instead of an LLM, no LLM, no embeddings; default zh prompt language (CJK character bigrams)
meow-memory.how: memory_remember.execute() per memory; ranked = memory_search.execute({query, k:10, explain:true}) (in-memory BM25 k1=1.5 b=0.75 over title+content+keywords with importance/recency weighting, ordered by bm25*recencyWeight); deployed = buildHitInjection(db, ws, sid, query, {}) = keywordHitScore over keywords of fact/lesson/rules/topic rows, hitTopK=2
notes: Package: meow-memory 0.32.6, the plugin's published lib/index.js imported unmodified; host peers stubbed: @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm (message constructors only, never used on this path); @deepseek-ai/schemastery installed from npm if available in the image build (see README).

memory_remember requires keywords (the LLM agent normally writes them). No LLM was used; keywords = all unique tokens of the memory text from the plugin's own exported tokenize(). With LLM-chosen keywords the deployed (keyword-hit) path would behave differently, probably with fewer but more curated keywords.

Tool has no date argument: Date.now() was set to each memory's date (12:00 UTC + index seconds) during ingest, and to the day after the last memory (2026-10-21) for all questions. Chosen before any run. Recency weighting (importance < 3 only, skipped for results scoring >= 85% of the best) therefore applies as it would to genuinely old memories.
All memories: level fact, project = global marker (so hit injection, which needs global scope or the session's current project, can see them), importance 1 (the tool's schema default), no title.

deployed = per-message keyword-hit injection (buildHitInjection, default hitTopK 2, no score threshold). The first-turn snapshot injects only soul/user levels and global rules with importance >= 2, which are not used here, so it returns no fact memories. deployed scores are rank-derived (2,1) because the function returns ids without scores. ms times buildHitInjection only (it reads rows from SQLite and tokenizes every candidate per call).

ranked = memory_search tool with k=10 and a fresh session per question (blind top-5 plus 5 unseen). The tool returns hits re-sorted by updated_at; the adapter restores retrieval order from explain.bm25 * explain.recencyWeight.

Usage stats (hit_count, last_accessed_at) are reset by direct SQL after each call so all questions see the same state; this only undoes the side effect of the lookup and does not influence ranking logic.
Dedup: memory_remember merges a new memory into an existing fact row when token Jaccard >= 0.8; merges: 0. A merged row maps to the newest memory id. Rows stored: 240 of 240 memories.
Write failures: 0. Question failures: 0. Returned items that could not be mapped to a memory id: 0.

caveat.zh: BM25 关键词检索；关键词由插件自带分词器生成（真实使用由 LLM 写关键词）；每条消息只按关键词命中注入前 2 条。
caveat.en: BM25 keyword retrieval; keywords come from the plugin's own tokenizer (in real use an LLM writes them); the per-message injection takes the top 2 keyword hits.

seekmemory-aged-detail.mode: verbatim ingest as level=detail memory artifacts via the kernel's persist(), no extraction, no embeddings (SeekMemory has no vector search), no LLM; deployed = recall.pipeline.query_block with default config (recall_k 8, budget 600 chars, evidence gate, disclosure); AGED: after ingest, clock advanced 365 days with zero recalls, maintain.decay.decay_all swept (240 memories forgotten), then the questions were answered
seekmemory-aged-detail.how: store.open_store(':memory:'); store.sources.append_sources([Source]); maintain.link.persist(make('memory', ...), artifacts, cache, graph); maintain.decay.decay_all(artifacts, cache, today); deployed: recall.pipeline.query_block(cache, graph, artifacts, sources, umo, text, private=True, conf=DEFAULTS, owner_umo, speaker, hybrid_retriever=HybridRetriever) -> info['final_ids']; ranked: HybridRetriever.retrieve + recall.score.select(k=10, gate=False, explore=0)
notes: decay_all(today=2027-11-14) marked 240 of 240 memories state=forgotten (reversible revision, row kept); no recall happened between ingest and the sweep.
Clock for the aged run: container date 2026-11-14 + 365 days = 2027-11-14; decay_all takes it as a parameter, recall.score/temporal/assemble `date` rebound for the run.

Write path: Source row (memory text, owner, one private session) + maintain.link.persist (commit + cache.put + link_new graph edges). Extraction is skipped because it needs an LLM; the artifact text is the memory text verbatim. No tags, no emotion values (defaults), shape=point, about=other, scope=private, said_by/subject_id=owner. The dataset fields source and kind were not given to the system.
level=detail was chosen before the first run: 'fact' is the level for plain statements; maintain.decay.decay_plan never forgets level=fact (maintain/expiry_policy.py:49-50).

Not applied because they need an extraction model: tags, arousal/valence, 'supersedes' (the only mechanism that retires an older memory when a newer one contradicts it). Updated questions therefore rely on ranking alone.

ids: the artifact id is the memory id; deployed ids come from info['final_ids'] (items that reached the assembled block, after the 600-char budget). Scores are rank-derived (1/rank) because select() and query_block return no scores; they carry no meaning across systems.

ranked: pool and scope-prior weighting replicate query_block; select(k=10, gate=False, explore=0). It bypasses the intent switch (intent 'none' for greetings/clock/operate words) and disclosure so it measures retrieval only. deployed keeps both.
deployed uses defaults including explore_rate 0.1 (seeded by the query text, may swap the last pick for a random lower-ranked one) and the recent-context fallback for profile/topic questions.
A persistent HybridRetriever is used (as in the host adapters); BM25 index builds on the warm-up query.

caveat.zh: 365 天老化实验，不是默认运行：记忆按 detail 级写入，老化后 240 条全部被标记为遗忘，什么都召回不到（Hit@5 0%，安静率 100%）。

seekmemory-aged.how: store.open_store(':memory:'); store.sources.append_sources([Source]); maintain.link.persist(make('memory', ...), artifacts, cache, graph); maintain.decay.decay_all(artifacts, cache, today); deployed: recall.pipeline.query_block(cache, graph, artifacts, sources, umo, text, private=True, conf=DEFAULTS, owner_umo, speaker, hybrid_retriever=HybridRetriever) -> info['final_ids']; ranked: HybridRetriever.retrieve + recall.score.select(k=10, gate=False, explore=0)
notes: decay_all(today=2027-11-14) marked 0 of 240 memories state=forgotten (reversible revision, row kept); no recall happened between ingest and the sweep.
Clock for the aged run: container date 2026-11-14 + 365 days = 2027-11-14; decay_all takes it as a parameter, recall.score/temporal/assemble `date` rebound for the run.

Write path: Source row (memory text, owner, one private session) + maintain.link.persist (commit + cache.put + link_new graph edges). Extraction is skipped because it needs an LLM; the artifact text is the memory text verbatim. No tags, no emotion values (defaults), shape=point, about=other, scope=private, said_by/subject_id=owner. The dataset fields source and kind were not given to the system.
level=fact was chosen before the first run: 'fact' is the level for plain statements; maintain.decay.decay_plan never forgets level=fact (maintain/expiry_policy.py:49-50).

Not applied because they need an extraction model: tags, arousal/valence, 'supersedes' (the only mechanism that retires an older memory when a newer one contradicts it). Updated questions therefore rely on ranking alone.

ids: the artifact id is the memory id; deployed ids come from info['final_ids'] (items that reached the assembled block, after the 600-char budget). Scores are rank-derived (1/rank) because select() and query_block return no scores; they carry no meaning across systems.

ranked: pool and scope-prior weighting replicate query_block; select(k=10, gate=False, explore=0). It bypasses the intent switch (intent 'none' for greetings/clock/operate words) and disclosure so it measures retrieval only. deployed keeps both.
deployed uses defaults including explore_rate 0.1 (seeded by the query text, may swap the last pick for a random lower-ranked one) and the recent-context fallback for profile/topic questions.
A persistent HybridRetriever is used (as in the host adapters); BM25 index builds on the warm-up query.
